newsitem.title: USA: Itron sees Q3 loss, revs below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Itron sees Q3 loss, revs below estimates.

text.p: Itron Inc said Wednesday its third quarter revenue will be significantly lower than anticipated and that it expects to report a loss for the quarter.

The company said revenue will fall short of forecasts primarily due to a "temporary industry-wide slow down in the pace of adding new automatic meter reading (AMR) orders and a pushout of shipments on a large multi-year AMR contract."
The combination of the slowdown and the company's "continued and increased investment in its development of fixed network technologies" will result in the loss, the company said.
First Call estimates project per-share net income of $0.20, compared with $0.20 per share in the year-ago period.

In a statement accompanying the announcement, the company's president said it has a "very sizeable" startup costs in its fixed-network AMR technology, and said it expects the business to be profitable in the beginning of 1998.

"The AMR market represents a multi-billion dollar opportunity which is in the early stages of development. The company estimates that approximately 10 million of the 235 million electric, gas and water meters in North America have AMR capabilities," said president Johnny Humphreys.
